svg.text: Read bottom-up: entry point → escalation bodies → apex. Arrows show escalation direction.
Apex judicial body · Treaty-established · Final authority on ecocide, Rights of Nature, Duty of Care breaches
Climate & Ecological Justice Tribunals (CJET) — specialized chamber within DJT
No further appeal — Rights of Nature violations

Coordinates biodiversity, oceans, animal welfare, food, water
GJO: oversees CJET · delegates enforcement to Shield Protocol
Duty of Care failures route through Planetary Duty of Care protocol → DJT
Provides Rights of Nature standards & scientific basis
MOS Dynamic Rights Spectrum informs ecocide threshold determinations
e.g. biodiversity vs animal welfare; oceans vs food systems
Earth Council guidance applies · unresolved → CJET
Monitors preparedness obligations under Duty of Care
Coordinates with Bioregional Grid Authorities & supply chains
Animal Welfare · Kinship Garden (Food) · Water & Sanitation
Inter-framework disputes escalate to PHC mediation
Failure to prepare → Duty of Care liability
e.g. mass ecosystem destruction · river personhood breach · species genocide
e.g. invasive species policy conflict · marine vs food system tension
e.g. preventable flood damage · governance body failed Duty of Care
⊘ Terminal — Rights of Nature violations end at CJET (within DJT), no further appeal
Advisory body — provides scientific/ethical standards but does not adjudicate
⚠ CJET is a specialized chamber within DJT, not a separate upstream body — this is structurally different from tech cluster.
PHC appears in two lanes (biodiversity oversight & disaster oversight) as it is the cross-cutting ecological coordination body.
Earth Council provides Indigenous wisdom guidance to PHC throughout. MOS Dynamic Rights Spectrum informs ecocide threshold determinations via Eco Intel.
